subject.title: Ensure transcript-to-client delivery consistency for channel-scoped sessions

question: What durable delivery-receipt contract should OpenClaw use for transcript-backed channel-scoped assistant outputs?
rationale: The next step chooses persistent schema, adapter reconciliation semantics, redelivery/idempotency rules, and UI/API exposure; code inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose those product and upgrade tradeoffs safely.

options.title: Design core receipt ledger first
options.body: Define the SQLite receipt schema, adapter reconciliation contract, transcript identity mapping, Gateway/session API, Control UI state, and duplicate-safe redelivery rules before implementation.

options.title: Land only the queue mitigation
options.body: Review the open mitigation PR for ambiguous no-reconciler queue entries while keeping this issue open for the broader transcript-to-provider ledger design.

options.title: Defer the reconciler
options.body: Keep current queue recovery and aggregate health behavior for now, accepting that transcript/client drift remains manually diagnosed.

recommendation.title: Design core receipt ledger first
recommendation.body: Define the SQLite receipt schema, adapter reconciliation contract, transcript identity mapping, Gateway/session API, Control UI state, and duplicate-safe redelivery rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest merged-history signal across the delivery queue substrate and recent outbound recovery hardening that the design would extend.
